actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed

facts.text: K-Bot is an open-source humanoid robot from K-Scale Labs
The project is in public alpha and the README warns that breaking changes are expected
The repository tracks ksim-kbot as a git submodule at path ksim-kbot with URL git@github.com:kscalelabs/ksim-kbot.git
The mechanical design notes say the hands can be swapped through a lens mount interface and use the same 48 volt power and CAN bus lines as the arm actuators

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and one ctrl sequence, so a trajectory repeats on the same engine; the model declares sensor noise elements, but this driver reads only the integration state and never reads a sensor. The bridge takes no seed input and a reset restores the model defaults, so no seed selects a different one. The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the served scene.mjcf with its robot.mjcf include, takes the actuator control ranges and the joint dimensions from that tree, then advances each actuated hinge by a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, equality, tendon or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result
the stand-in loads no mesh, texture or heightfield and resolves no contact or friction: the scene's heightfield floor and the robot's collision geoms are not simulated
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
snapshots copy time, qpos, qvel, act and ctrl (the bridge's fallback) because the stand-in offers no mj_getState/mj_setState/mj_stateSize; a restore is not the full integration state of MuJoCo
no physical K-Bot is modelled and nothing was validated against the K-Scale hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
